title: Hydrocarbons
summary: Learn the structure, naming and reactions of alkanes, alkenes, alkynes and benzene.
cards.0.p: Compounds made only of carbon and hydrogen are called hydrocarbons. Aliphatic hydrocarbons have no benzene ring. They are the single-bonded alkanes, the double-bonded alkenes and the triple-bonded alkynes. Aromatic hydrocarbons contain a benzene ring.
cards.0.key: Natural gas and crude oil are their main sources. If the structure contains O, N or Cl, it is no longer a hydrocarbon.
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: It contains only C and H.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: It contains oxygen, so it is not a hydrocarbon.
cards.0.once.secenekler.2.neden: It contains chlorine, so it is not a hydrocarbon.
cards.1.p: Alkanes contain only single bonds and are saturated with hydrogen. Their general formula is CnH2n+2. Methane through butane are gases, and pentane through decane are liquids. Their names end in -ane.
cards.1.svg#0: The first 10 alkanes (n = number of C)
cards.1.key: By number of carbons, the roots are meth, eth, prop, but, pent, hex, hept, oct, non and dec.
cards.2.p: First find the longest chain and number it from the end nearest the branch. Write the branch with its number, as methyl, ethyl and so on. Add di- or tri- for repeated branches. Different branches are written in alphabetical order.
cards.2.svg#18: branch position – branch name + parent chain name
cards.2.key: 2,2-dimethylpropane and 3-ethyl-2-methylpentane are examples. A Cl branch is written as chloro. The branch must get the lowest number. So it is 2-methylbutane, not 3-methylbutane.
cards.3.p: Alkane molecules attract each other only through London forces. As the chain gets longer, the boiling point rises. For the same formula, more branching means a smaller contact surface and a lower boiling point.
cards.3.etk.soru: Order these alkanes from lowest to highest boiling point.
cards.3.key: Alkanes are nonpolar, do not dissolve in water and are lighter than water. Straight alkanes with C₁₈ or more are solids. Paraffin wax is a mixture of them.
cards.4.p: Alkanes are not very reactive. With enough oxygen, they burn and give CO2 and H2O. With too little oxygen, toxic CO forms. In light, a halogen atom replaces an H atom.
cards.4.svg#2: propane in a gas tank: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O
cards.4.svg#15: H leaves, Cl enters. If it continues: CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃, CCl₄
cards.4.key: Because alkanes are saturated, they undergo substitution, not addition.
cards.5.p: If the two ends of a chain join, a cycloalkane forms. The general formula of cycloalkanes is CnH2n, and they are saturated. Cyclopropane has narrow angles, so it is strained and reactive. Cyclohexane is stable.
cards.5.svg#6: Skeletal formula: each corner is a CH₂
cards.5.svg#7: C₃H₆: cyclopropane and propene are isomers
cards.5.key: Bromine water tells cyclohexane apart from an alkene. Under suitable conditions, though, cyclopropane can add Br₂.
cards.5.once.soru: If the two ends of hexane (C₆H₁₄) join to form a ring, what is the formula?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: As the ends join, each end loses one H. So the ring has two fewer H atoms.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: When the end carbons bond to each other, each must give up one H.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: The ring removes only two H atoms, and the single bonds stay.
cards.6.p: Alkenes contain a C=C double bond and are unsaturated. Their general formula is CnH2n. Their names use -ene instead of -ane, as in ethene and propene. Numbering starts from the end nearest the double bond.
cards.6.svg#22: Numbering starts from the end nearest the double bond.
cards.6.key: 1-butene and 2-butene are position isomers. Their formulas are the same, but the double bond is in a different place.
cards.6.once.soru: Ethene's formula is C₂H₄, and ethane's is C₂H₆. What is different in ethene?
cards.6.once.secenekler.0.neden: When two carbons are joined by a double bond, there is no room left for two H atoms.
cards.6.once.secenekler.1.neden: Two carbons cannot form a ring.
cards.6.once.secenekler.2.neden: Both contain only C and H.
cards.7.p: In 2-butene, if the two CH3 groups are on the same side of the double bond, it is the cis isomer. If they are on opposite sides, it is the trans isomer. They are different substances with different boiling points.
cards.7.svg#16: Condition: each of the two C atoms carries two different groups
cards.7.key: Cis-2-butene boils at about 4 °C and trans-2-butene at about 1 °C. This is because the cis isomer is slightly polar.
cards.7.once.soru: A double bond cannot rotate. In 2-butene, the two CH₃ groups can sit on the same side or on opposite sides. Are these the same substance?
cards.7.once.secenekler.0.neden: The bond that cannot rotate keeps the two arrangements apart. So two isomers with different properties form.
cards.7.once.secenekler.1.neden: Around a single bond, rotation would change the arrangement. Around a double bond, there is no rotation.
cards.7.once.secenekler.2.neden: The difference lies in the molecule's structure, not in its state.
cards.8.p: One of the bonds in the double bond opens, and one atom is added to each of the two carbons. This is called addition. Adding H2 gives an alkane. Adding Br2 makes bromine water lose its color.
cards.8.svg#21: Markovnikov: H goes to the C with more H, Br to the middle C
cards.8.key: When HX adds, the H bonds to the carbon that already has more hydrogens (Markovnikov's rule). For example, propene and HBr give 2-bromopropane.
cards.9.h: Polymerization: from ethene to plastic bags
cards.9.p: The double bonds of thousands of ethene molecules open, and the molecules join end to end to form polyethylene. The small unit is called a monomer, and the giant molecule a polymer. No double bonds remain in the polymer.
cards.9.key: PVC is made from vinyl chloride, and Teflon from tetrafluoroethene.
cards.9.once.soru: Polyethylene, the plastic in shopping bags, is made from which small molecule?
cards.9.once.secenekler.0.neden: Ethene's double bond opens, and the molecules join end to end.
cards.9.once.secenekler.1.neden: Methane is saturated and has no double bond to open.
cards.9.once.secenekler.2.neden: The benzene ring is stable, and it is not the unit of polyethylene.
cards.10.p: Alkynes contain a C≡C triple bond, and their general formula is CnH2n−2. The simplest alkyne is ethyne (acetylene), C2H2. When ethyne burns in oxygen, it gives a welding flame above 3000 °C.
cards.10.svg#14: 1 mol of ethyne is fully saturated by 2 mol of H₂
cards.10.key: Addition to alkynes happens in two steps: the alkyne first becomes an alkene, then an alkane. 1 mol of alkyne uses 2 mol of H₂ or 2 mol of Br₂. 1 mol of alkene uses 1 mol.
cards.11.h: Naming alkynes and the terminal alkyne test
cards.11.p: Alkyne names end in -yne, as in ethyne, propyne and 1-butyne. If the triple bond is at the end of the chain, it is a terminal alkyne. Terminal alkynes give a precipitate with ammoniacal AgNO3.
cards.11.svg#0: Name: alkane root + -yne · ethyne, propyne, butyne
cards.11.key: 2-butyne gives no precipitate. So this test tells a terminal alkyne apart from an internal one. CuCl also gives a precipitate.
cards.11.once.soru: 1-butyne and 2-butyne have the same formula. Which one has ≡C–H at its end?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: The triple bond is at carbon 1, and the end carbon carries an H.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: The triple bond is in the middle, and both ends carry CH₃.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: In 2-butyne, the triple bond is not at the end.
cards.12.p: In benzene (C6H6), 6 π electrons spread around the ring (delocalized), and all the C–C bonds are equal. Because of this stability, benzene undergoes substitution instead of addition.
cards.12.key: Toluene is aromatic too. On a ring with two groups, the positions are called ortho (1,2), meta (1,3) and para (1,4).
cards.13.p: Gasoline is made of C5–C10 hydrocarbons separated from crude oil. Early ignition in an engine is called knocking. Resistance to knocking is measured by the octane rating. Branched alkanes have high octane ratings.
cards.13.svg#1: More branching means a higher octane rating.
cards.13.key: Isooctane is set at 100 and n-heptane at 0. 95-octane gasoline behaves like 95% isooctane + 5% n-heptane.
cards.13.once.soru: The pump says "95 octane". What does the octane rating show?
cards.13.once.secenekler.0.neden: High-octane gasoline does not ignite too early in the engine.
cards.13.once.secenekler.1.neden: Gasolines have similar energy. The octane rating measures resistance to early ignition.
cards.13.once.secenekler.2.neden: Sulfur is measured separately. The octane rating shows resistance to knocking.
cards.14.p:
• Alkanes contain single bonds, alkenes double bonds and alkynes triple bonds.
• A longer alkane chain raises the boiling point, and branching lowers it.
• Alkanes and benzene undergo substitution. Alkenes and alkynes undergo addition and decolorize bromine water.
• For cis-trans isomerism, both carbons of the double bond must carry different groups.
quiz.0.q: How many moles of O₂ are used when 1 mol of butane (C₄H₁₀) burns completely?
quiz.0.e: C₄H₁₀ + 6.5O₂ → 4CO₂ + 5H₂O. 4 CO₂ need 8 O, and 5 H₂O need 5 O. That is 13 O atoms in total, or 6.5 mol of O₂.
quiz.1.q: Sort each hydrocarbon as saturated or unsaturated.
quiz.1.e: Alkanes and cycloalkanes contain only single bonds and are saturated. Alkenes, ending in -ene, have C=C, and alkynes, ending in -yne, have C≡C. These are unsaturated.
quiz.2.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH(C₂H₅)–CH₂–CH₂–CH₃?
quiz.2.e: The longest chain has 6 C (hexane). Numbering from the end nearest the branches puts methyl on carbon 2 and ethyl on carbon 3. Branches are written in alphabetical order, so the name is 3-ethyl-2-methylhexane.
quiz.2.y.0: Branches are written in alphabetical order. So ethyl (e) comes before methyl (m).
quiz.2.y.2: Numbering starts from the end nearest a branch. The set 2,3 is lower than 4,5.
quiz.2.y.3: The parent chain has 6 C. You also need to include the CH₂–CH₂–CH₃ end on the right.
quiz.3.e: In 2-butene, each double-bonded carbon carries two different groups (CH₃ and H). In the others, at least one double-bonded carbon carries two H atoms. So not every alkene shows cis-trans isomerism.
quiz.3.y.0: In ethene, each carbon carries two H atoms. A carbon with two identical groups does not show cis-trans isomerism.
quiz.3.y.1: In propene, the end carbon carries two H atoms. Geometric isomerism needs different groups on each carbon of the double bond.
quiz.3.y.2: In 1-butene, the double bond is at the end and C1 carries two H atoms. So it has no cis-trans isomers.
A:ozet: Grow the alkane series and boil branched isomers. Find the longest chain, saturate ethyne, test with bromine water and burn pentane.
A:adimlar.0.metin: Alkanes contain only single bonds, and their general formula is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Increase the number of carbons and watch the boiling point. Find the first alkane that is a liquid at room temperature.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.ipucu: Look for the first alkane whose boiling point passes the 25 °C line.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.tamam: Pentane boils at 36 °C. As the chain gets longer, London forces grow and the boiling point rises.
A:adimlar.1.metin: In naming, the longest chain gives the parent name (pentane for 5 C). The branch is numbered from the nearest end. Bend the chain and count the carbons.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.soru: What is the IUPAC name of this alkane?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: The longest chain has 5 C (pentane), and the methyl branch is on carbon 3 from either end. The molecule's formula is C₆H₁₄, so it is an isomer of hexane.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The horizontal chain has 4 C, but it is not the longest chain. The ethyl branch continues the chain, and including it gives 5 C.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Both the chain and the number are wrong. The longest chain has 5 C, and the branch must get the lowest number.
A:adimlar.2.metin: Three containers hold three alkanes with the same formula (C₅H₁₂). One has a straight chain, one has one branch, and one has two branches. We heat all three slowly together.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Pentane has a straight chain. Its molecules touch along a long surface, so London attraction is strongest. That is why it boils last (36 °C).
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: The most branched molecule is the closest to a sphere. Its contact surface is small, and London attraction is weak. So it boils first, at 10 °C.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: The molar mass is the same, but the shape differs. Branching shrinks the contact surface and lowers the boiling point.
A:adimlar.3.metin: Ethyne (C₂H₂) has a triple bond. Each mole of H₂ opens one π bond and adds one H to each of the two carbons. Saturate ethyne completely.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.ipucu: A triple bond has two π bonds.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.tamam: The alkyne first becomes an alkene, then an alkane. So addition happens in two steps.
A:adimlar.4.metin: Three tubes hold orange bromine water. We add a few drops of a hydrocarbon to each and shake.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.soru: In which tube does the bromine water lose its color?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Hexane is saturated, and Br₂ cannot add to its single bonds. In light, slow substitution happens, but the color does not disappear right away.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Benzene is drawn with double bonds, but its stable aromatic ring resists addition. So the color stays.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Hexene's C=C bond opens, and Br₂ adds to the two carbons. The colored Br₂ is used up, so the color fades. This is a test for unsaturation.
A:adimlar.5.metin: Benzene is drawn as if it had three double bonds, but those bonds do not stay in place. Show the ring and look at the bond lengths.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: Why doesn't benzene decolorize bromine water?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: C₆H₆ has 8 fewer H atoms than hexane (C₆H₁₄), which has the same number of carbons, so it is not saturated. The difference is that its π electrons spread around the ring.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.yazi: The spread-out π ring is very stable
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Addition would break the aromatic ring, so benzene undergoes substitution instead. With an FeBr₃ catalyst, Br₂ replaces an H.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Benzene has 6 π electrons. They are not in fixed double bonds but spread over the whole ring.
A:adimlar.6.metin: When pentane (C₅H₁₂) burns, CO₂ and H₂O form. Balance the equation with the O₂ coefficient.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.ipucu: How many O atoms are on the right? Each O₂ brings two O.
A:adimlar.6.gorev.tamam: C₅H₁₂ + 8O₂ → 5CO₂ + 6H₂O. With too little oxygen, combustion is incomplete, and toxic CO and soot form. Combustion is a redox reaction.
A:kapanis.0: The formula of alkanes is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. They have single bonds and are saturated. A longer chain raises the boiling point, and branching lowers it.
A:kapanis.1: The name comes from the longest chain, and numbering starts from the end nearest a branch. 3-methylpentane is named this way.
A:kapanis.2: An alkyne first becomes an alkene, then an alkane. 1 mol of alkyne adds 2 mol of H₂ or Br₂, and 1 mol of alkene adds 1 mol.
A:kapanis.3: Alkenes and alkynes decolorize bromine water. Alkanes and benzene do not.
A:kapanis.4: Benzene's 6 π electrons are spread around the ring. Because of this stability, benzene undergoes substitution instead of addition.
